description: Start a new presentation from a brief, the brand and your outline. The brand: if you can open the brand's website, read its real colours and fonts there first and declare them — the lead colour is usually the main buttons and the large coloured areas, not the link colour — and always give the website; never invent a colour. With the outline the reply carries PAGE 1'S BRIEF; write page 1 and send it with submit_page — each reply carries the next page's brief. Without an account it also returns a guest_token to pass on later calls and deck_url, the one link to give the user.

brand.description: The brand as YOU know it: name, and only the colours, fonts and logo you actually have. Never guess a colour; leave it out.

accent.description: The lead brand colour (usually the main buttons and the large coloured areas, not the links), only if you know it from the user, their material or their site. Never invent one.

background.description: The page background colour, only if known.

body.description: Body font family name, only if known.

headline.description: Headline font family name, only if known.

logo_url.description: A public https image of the logo (SVG or PNG), only if you have a real one.

name.description: The brand's name as it should appear.

text.description: The main text colour, only if known.

voice.description: How the brand speaks, in a sentence or two.

website.description: Their website, e.g. yourcompany.com. With an account, when you declare no colours, Renderball reads the site for its colours, fonts and logo — so give the website and leave colours you do not know out.

brand_url.description: Key holders only: a website Renderball reads for colours, fonts and logo when no brand is declared.

brief.description: What the deck is for, who it is for, what it should argue and ask. Real facts only; the truth check refuses invented figures.

outline.description: Your page-by-page outline (one entry per page: label, description, visual_concept, content with a headline). Send it here and the reply carries the brief to write from (page 1's brief when the deck is written page by page) — one call instead of create_deck + write_outline.

content.description: The approved copy. Every numeral here must come from the user's material — the deck's truth check enforces it.

bullets.description: Up to 6 short points; no walls.

caption.description: Small mono caption, e.g. a source line.

eyebrow.description: Tiny label above the headline, e.g. 'THE PROBLEM'.

meta.description: Stat tiles as label/value pairs — ONLY figures the user gave you.

description.description: What this page must accomplish in the argument, one or two sentences. Not shown on the page.

label.description: Short page title, 2-6 words (e.g. 'The Tracker Tax').

visual_concept.description: The composition and the one graphic device that expresses the page's argument: layout, the diagram/chart/mock, where the headline sits, colours by role. Concrete enough to draw from.

pages.description: How many pages you intend to write (default 5). Ignored when `outline` is given.

name: create_deck
title: Create a deck
